title: No tricks, just treats
caption: The barred spiral galaxy M83, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: M83 · constellation Hydra · about 15 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, A. Adamo (Stockholm University) and the FEAST JWST team

recognition.text: Ranked #91 on ESA/Webb’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: Two spiral arms reach sideways from a barred galaxy's core and merge into a broad network of gas and dust that fills the frame, glowing bright orange along the arms and darker red elsewhere. Through gaps in the dust, countless tiny stars show, packed most densely around the core. This is M83, also known as NGC 5236, about 15 million light-years away in Hydra, seen by Webb's MIRI.

MIRI observes mid-infrared light between 5 and 28 micrometers, far beyond the roughly 0.38 to 0.75 micrometers our eyes respond to. It doesn't take in that whole range at once. It has ten filters, each passing a narrow slice. This image uses just two, near the short end.

Bright blue shows stars across the central galaxy, yellow marks active stellar nurseries threading the arms, and orange-red traces carbon-based molecules called polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, which one of the two filters is especially good at imaging.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (5.89 x 1.87 arcminutes) and distance (15 million light years), the frame spans roughly 26,000 × 8,200 light-years. Its light set out about 15 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Webb's Mid-Infrared Instrument used two filters. Blue shows stars, yellow stellar nurseries and orange-red PAH molecules.
understand.eye: Mid-infrared light lies well outside the range the human eye can see.

behind.processing: Colors assigned by filter, as listed.

explore: M83 was observed in the FEAST program, whose six galaxies, M51 among them, were all imaged with both NIRCam and MIRI, two of Webb's four instruments. As an example of how narrow the filters are, F770W passes only light between 6.581 and 8.687 micrometers.
alt: A barred spiral galaxy with two arms reaching sideways into a network of orange and dark red gas and dust, with countless tiny stars visible through the gaps, densest at the core.
